About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

The IT Operations team keeps Anthropic running — we make sure every employee can do their best work without friction. We're seeking an IT Support Engineer who combines deep technical skills with a genuine service mindset and sound judgment.
Anthropic is growing fast, and our IT operations need to keep pace. That means onboarding at scale, automating repetitive processes (including with Claude), and continuously improving the employee experience. You'll handle support challenges across our primarily macOS environment while contributing to the operational improvements that help us scale. You'll work closely with IT Engineering and Security, with opportunities to grow into more technical infrastructure work over time.

End-User Support
Triage and resolve issues across hardware, software, networking, and accounts — primarily through our ticketing system, with additional support via Slack and in-person
Diagnose and resolve issues across macOS, ChromeOS, iOS, Android, and our core SaaS platforms (Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub, Atlassian)
Troubleshoot device issues, including enrollment, configuration profiles, and policy enforcement
Support access management and employee lifecycle workflows (onboarding, offboarding, reorgs)
Handle escalations requiring cross-team coordination
Participate in an on-call rotation for urgent issues outside business hours
Provide hands-on support for user technology, AV systems, conference rooms, and printers
Communication & Documentation
Communicate clearly with users of all technical levels
Write and maintain internal documentation including runbooks, how-to guides, and knowledge base articles
Identify patterns in support requests, surface recurring issues to the team, and identify opportunities for automation or systemic solves
Operational Improvement
Help streamline onboarding and other high-volume operations as the company scales
Contribute to automation efforts
Maintain and improve device management, identity, and access systems
Assist with scripting (Bash, Python) to automate repetitive tasks
You may be a good fit if you
Have 7+ years of hands-on IT support experience, ideally in a fast-paced or high-growth environment
Are an excellent communicator who genuinely enjoys helping people solve problems
Have strong troubleshooting skills and are methodical, curious, and persistent
Demonstrated supporting macOS endpoints and comfortable supporting ChromeOS, iOS, and Android
Have significant experience with Google Workspace administration
Have experience with Slack administration — workspace management, permissions, and troubleshooting
Have substantial experience supporting and administering additional SaaS tools
Understand identity and access fundamentals — SSO, MFA, directory services
Are familiar with MDM fundamentals and endpoint management concepts
Have experience with basic scripting (Bash or Python) for automation
Take ownership of problems and follow through until they're resolved
Think beyond the immediate fix — you ask "why did this happen?" and "how do we prevent it?"
Are organized enough to manage competing priorities without things falling through the cracks
Propose solutions when you see a process that doesn't scale
Are looking to develop deeper technical skills and take on more complex systems administration challenges over time

Have experience with networking basics — DNS, DHCP, VPNs, networking fundamentals
Have contributed to IT projects beyond day-to-day support (migrations, tool rollouts, process redesigns)

You'll be joining a high-impact IT team supporting some of the world's leading AI researchers and engineers. The pace is fast and you'll have real ownership over your work. Because we're scaling rapidly, you'll have meaningful opportunities to shape how IT operations work at Anthropic.

We're looking for a Manager, IT Support to lead our Americas support team. IT Support is the front door for every employee technology need at Anthropic: our Claude-backed support assistant, the human ticket queue behind it, walk-ups and desk-side help, hardware swaps, conference room triage, and a dedicated white-glove channel for our executives and board.
This is first and foremost a people leadership role. You'll manage a team of IT Support Engineers across San Francisco, New York, and Seattle—hiring them, coaching them, and growing them.
The role goes beyond running a queue, too. Our support model is being rebuilt this year, and much of what you'd normally inherit doesn't exist yet—you'll help shape the service levels this team is held to, and stand up the Americas leg of a follow-the-sun on-call rotation.

You'll also hold a tension we take seriously: our engineers build the automation that keeps requests from ever reaching a person, and they treat the queue as the first priority, always.

You'll partner closely with our specialist operations teams, IT Engineering, Security, People Operations, and Workplace to deliver an exceptional employee experience while maintaining the rigorous security posture our mission demands.

Lead, coach, and develop a team of IT Support Engineers across San Francisco, New York, and Seattle—1:1s, feedback, performance management, and career growth
Hire IT Support Engineers, including for our executive and board support function, and raise the bar as the team grows
Own in-office coverage and staffing across San Francisco, New York, and Seattle, and lead a team you aren't always in the same room with
Own queue health, service level attainment, and routing rules across the Americas
Be accountable for how the Americas performs against our support metrics—first-touch resolution, time to first response, time to resolution, employee satisfaction—and drive the changes that move them
Run and staff the Americas on-call rotation within the global follow-the-sun model
Route escalations into specialist operations teams and IT Engineering, and hold your team to those boundaries
Protect engineering time for automation and deflection work without letting the queue slip
Collaborate with Workplace, People Ops, and other teams to support office operations and company events
Travel regularly to San Francisco and occasionally to Seattle
You may be a good fit if you have
7+ years of experience in IT support and operations, with 3+ years managing a support team
A track record of managing and developing engineers: hiring, coaching, performance conversations that change behavior, and moving people into their next role
Experience leading a frontline IT support team, including ownership of a queue, its service levels, and the people who work it
Experience managing across multiple offices, including reports you don't sit with, and a real answer for how you keep them developing
Strong hands-on IT support fundamentals: macOS-primary fleets, identity and access, SaaS troubleshooting, hardware lifecycle, and AV first-response
A demonstrated ability to move a support function's metrics
A security-first mindset and excellent judgment about when user experience yields to security requirements
Comfort with ambiguity and rapidly shifting priorities in a fast-paced environment
Strong written communication—you can write a runbook, a postmortem, and a piece of hard feedback, and have each land
Strong candidates may also have
Experience building support infrastructure rather than inheriting it: a queue structure, an on-call rotation, an escalation model, or SLAs that didn't exist before you arrived
Experience supporting executives or a board to a white-glove standard
Experience building support automation, ticket deflection programs, or self-service platforms
Experience supporting AI/ML research environments or highly technical user bases
Background in companies with significant security or compliance requirements (e.g. SOC 2, FedRAMP)
Location
This role is based in our New York City office and we expect you to be in-office 3 days per week.

We are looking for an experienced, hands-on support leader to build and run the support and escalation motion for GPT-Rosalind and OpenAI’s life sciences customers.
This is both a builder role and a frontline support role. You will work directly with customers, own complex cases, diagnose technical and operational issues, and coordinate cross-functional teams through resolution. You will also create the intake paths, playbooks, knowledge, tooling, and operating mechanisms needed to support life sciences workflows across ChatGPT, Codex, and the OpenAI API.
You’ll partner closely with Account Directors, Product, Engineering and Forward Deployed Engineering, Security, Legal, and bioscience subject-matter experts. You will help customers receive coordinated, accurate answers while maintaining clear boundaries between technical support, scientific consultation, product feedback, and roadmap commitments.
This role is an opportunity to define how OpenAI supports scientists and life sciences organizations as they adopt increasingly capable AI systems.

Work directly with Rosalind and life sciences customers, taking ownership of complex technical and operational support cases from intake through resolution.
Serve as a critical escalation point and final line of defense for complex technical issues, partnering closely with customers and Engineering teams to troubleshoot, resolve, and proactively prevent recurring problems while leveraging scripting and emerging AI capabilities to improve internal tooling and automate operational workflows
Support customer workflows across ChatGPT, Codex, and the OpenAI API, including questions about tool access, environment constraints, reproducibility, product behavior, and responsible model usage.
Build bioscience-aware intake flows, diagnostic procedures, routing logic, escalation paths, playbooks, response templates, and internal and customer-facing knowledge content.
Determine whether an issue requires technical support, workflow enablement, scientific consultation, solutions architecture, product feedback, or another specialized response, and route it to the appropriate owner without losing context or accountability.
Coordinate complex escalations across Product, Engineering, Forward Deployed Engineering, Security, Legal, Account Directors, and bioscience subject-matter experts, providing clear handoffs and driving cases through closure.
Maintain appropriate boundaries around scientific guidance: support standard Rosalind usage and technical workflows while engaging qualified bioscience experts for novel scientific consultation, research optimization, or domain-specific validity judgments.
Identify recurring issues across scientific workflows, specialized tooling, access and provisioning, governance, and product usage, then turn those patterns into durable fixes, better documentation, and product improvements.
Build a repeatable customer-feedback loop that captures and synthesizes bugs, product gaps, and unmet needs for the Rosalind, Product, and Engineering teams.
Use AI, automation, and lightweight technical solutions to improve triage, routing, case summarization, knowledge management, and support quality.
Help define the long-term operating model, service levels, coverage requirements, and specialization strategy for biosciences support.
Foster a supportive, rigorous, and customer-focused culture within User Operations.

Background managing complex, customer facing support cases end to end, from initial inquiry and triage through reproduction, escalation, and resolution.

As a IT SPECIALIST (PLCYPLN), GS-2210-11, you will perform the following duties: 1. Information Technology Planning: (a) Analyzes requirements and establishes plans of action for improving IT applications. Analyzes existing and planned IT applications, both hardware and software, to determine current and future potential for enhancements.

Based upon the organization's goals and objectives, an assessment of available resources, and extrapolation of cost benefit analysis data, recommends adjustments to IT priorities to meet changing business needs, program plans, goals and objectives.

Develops project plans to meet those needs by identifying problem areas and considering a variety of possible solutions and alternatives. Analyzes existing systems to determine if enhancements are appropriate or if an entirely new system would be more cost effective.

Analyzes plans and specifications, prepares justifications for new or enhanced information technology. Coordinates results of analysis with impacted organizations to ensure compatibility with existing architecture and recommends proposals to reduce conflicts.

Develops milestones and performs as point of contact throughout the various phases of projects until successfully concluded. (b) Performs as plans and policy advisor to functional users of information technology. Develops and interprets policy for administering IT systems.

Assesses policy needs and reviews, revises, and develops policies to govern IT activities and presents recommendations to higher-level management. Where necessary, modifies established plans and policies in response to changes in legislation or other directives.

Through feasibility studies, assesses impact of changes on current programs and recommends changes to existing plans to ensure compliance. This includes long range planning, and involves defining current and future business requirements.

Analyzes IT system development as it relates to the organization and ensures policy and guidance are available for its use, that necessary controls are in place, and systems operate as intended and provide all necessary capabilities. Develops migration plans for implementation of new technology.

Assesses and identifies training needs that address activities where gaps in competency exist in either current or new technology. Develops training programs, or locates and recommends sources of training that ensure users can apply the best techniques in using IT. Provides technical assistance to system users and contractors.

This includes keeping abreast of the latest developments in technology and conducting feasibility studies to evaluate systems performance as it relates to the organization. 2. Telecommunications Planning: Plans and develops methods, procedures, policies, and techniques concerning telecommunication systems.

Performs work involved in developing, refining, and complying with telecommunications systems planning and policy direction including short- and/or long-range planning.

Develops planning documentation, reviews requests for communication services, prepares budgetary justifications, coordinates the allocation of resources, designs networks/systems, prepares/reviews equipment and facility specifications, monitors/resolves technical communications problems, and/or conducts operational acceptance tests.

May serve in a liaison capacity between contractors and wing officials to resolve a wide variety of conventional problems involving high value telecommunication systems. Develops implementing instructions. 3. General IT and Communications Planning and Resourcing: (a) Implements IT and communications programs and special projects.

Implements various IT and communications programs. Updates documentation and maintains listings of all authorized equipment for assigned programs. Performs annual inventories. Performs special staff and/or feasibility studies and economic analysis. May serve on committees or planning groups concerned with future systems, plans, and policy.

(b) Assists with contracting functions and budget preparation. Upon completion of feasibility studies and other projects designed to identify functional needs and changing business requirements for advancements in technology, prepares budgetary data for inclusion in financial plans in support of programs and projects.

Based upon findings, recommends funding priority adjustments to meet new business needs. Conducts periodic analysis of projects and their funding for consistency with overall IT and communications architecture and infrastructure and how they contribute to meeting business requirements.

The Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts, Case Management Modernization (CMM) Program Office seeks a skilled and self-motivated Test Data Manager. The Test Data Manager plans, provisions, and governs test data sets that enable reliable functional, regression, and user acceptance testing (UAT) across CMM.

Additionally, the Test Data Manager coordinates with build pods to supply data ready for UAT, aligns test data practices to environment needs, and supports quality gates by ensuring test data is available, traceable, and appropriate for the intended testing purpose.

The duties of this position include, but are not limited to: Defining and executing CMM's test data approach across environments, including refresh cadence, provisioning workflows, definitions, evidence expectations, and dataset versioning.

Coordinating with data platform and integration teams to generate, transform, and stage test datasets aligned to build pod requirements and UAT plans. Implementing safeguards for sensitive data usage in test environments, including synthetic/anonymized data practices where required.

Maintaining test data inventories and requesting intake so pod teams can access the right datasets for sprint testing and regression coverage. Resolving test data defects (missing values, referential gaps, stale extracts) and partnering with engineering colleagues to prevent recurring issues.

Providing UAT data and coordinating data readiness checkpoints as part of broader release readiness activities. Developing standards of operation for handling and archiving data. Evaluating the design, selection, and implementation of database changes to ensure data integrity and security.

Ensuring data and information security by integrating and upholding digital security systems.

Maintaining test data inventories, including resolving test data defects (missing values, referential gaps, stale extracts), and partnering with engineering colleagues to prevent recurring issues. Preferred qualifications include experience: Managing enterprise test data strategies across multiple environments and teams.

Data masking, synthetic data generation, and controlled access patterns. Collaborating with data engineering, integration, and application delivery teams. Creating clear, auditable test data documentation and operational procedures. Databases and data formats (SQL, CSV, XML, JSON).

Atticus is hiring an IT Specialist to own and mature our internal IT operations as we scale.

You’ll work closely with and report to the Information Security Manager, supporting day-to-day IT operations while helping improve the systems, processes, and tooling we rely on across endpoint device lifecycle management, identity and access, SaaS administration, and our broader cloud-first IT environment.

About us Atticus is a Melbourne-based scale-up founded in 2017, which offers the leading technology in document fact-checking. We are on a mission to ensure every critical document is accurate and defensible. Our software helps our customers (law firms, listed companies, and funds) fact-check critical documents before they are disclosed to market.

Our users love Atticus because we save them a lot of pain in high stakes work. We are a small, highly efficient team that relies on well-run internal systems to stay productive. As we grow, we are committed to preserving that speed while maintaining the security, reliability, and trust our customers expect.

That means giving our people simple, dependable tools and support, while ensuring our devices, access, and SaaS systems are managed in a secure and scalable way. About the role As our IT Specialist, you will keep Atticus ’s internal IT operations running smoothly while helping us build a more scalable, secure, and reliable technology environment.

You’ll act as a first point of contact with users, manage devices and access, improve integrations between platforms, and ensure our internal tools are reliable, secure, and easy to use. As a small and highly efficient company, this is a broad role suited to someone comfortable operating across multiple areas of IT.

You’ll need to take initiative, solve ambiguous or unfamiliar problems, follow through reliably, and balance responsive support with longer-term improvement work. From time to time, the role may involve after-hours support for our UK team, particularly for onboarding, offboarding, or urgent support needs.

You will also be accountable for driving the pace of projects that strengthen how we manage identity, devices, applications, data, and access. You’ll be working across a range of responsibilities that support the smooth running and ongoing improvement of our internal IT operations:

Internal IT support: Providing end-to-end technical support across user devices, applications, account access, and collaboration tools, helping staff resolve issues quickly with minimal disruption to their work.

Endpoint lifecycle management: Managing the full lifecycle of endpoint devices — primarily that our Apple fleet is consistently enrolled, configured, patched, and compliant, with a repeatable and well-documented lifecycle process from procurement through to retirement.

Apple device management & automation: Writing and maintaining scripts to support macOS administration, MDM workflows, app deployment, and compliance checks, improving consistency and scalability as we grow.

Identity & access management: Managing accounts, permissions, and access changes are managed accurately and promptly, onboarding and offboarding workflows are automated, and our IAM practices mature in line with the needs of the business.

SaaS & business systems administration: Managing and optimising core SaaS platforms to keep them reliable, secure, and well-integrated, while improving visibility and governance across the application stack.

Process improvement & automation: Identifying, prioritising, and improving manual IT processes to create faster workflows, reduce errors, and support a more scalable IT operation.

Security-aligned operations: Partnering with the Information Security Manager to ensure IT operations support broader security objectives across devices, users, applications, and access.

Documentation: Developing and maintaining technical documentation, runbooks, and user guides for end users, IT/security stakeholders, and future team members.
About you We’re looking for a capable and proactive IT professional with 3+ years of experience in IT, systems administration, endpoint management, IT operations, or a similar role. You enjoy helping people solve practical technology problems, but also care about improving the systems, processes, and automation that reduce friction over time.

You have a strong sense of ownership, are comfortable working independently in a broad role, and are looking for an opportunity to take greater ownership of a modern, cloud-first internal IT environment.

You have hands-on experience managing user devices, access, SaaS platforms, and identity-related tooling, and are comfortable balancing responsive support with longer-term improvement work.

You do not need to have worked with every tool we use, but you should be practical, curious, technically confident, and willing to learn unfamiliar systems when needed. So if you’ve got the following skills and capabilities then please get in touch:

Internal IT & user support: Experience providing end-to-end technical support across hardware, software, accounts, collaboration tools, and internal systems, including troubleshooting, escalations, and Apple device support.

Endpoint & device management: Solid understanding of endpoint management in macOS and Apple environments, including MDM, device enrolment, configuration, app deployment, patching, compliance, and the full device lifecycle.

Apple administration & scripting: Strong working knowledge of macOS administration with the ability to write or maintain scripts for Apple/Unix environments to support MDM workflows, app deployment, reporting, and repeatable IT operations.

Identity & access management: Experience managing identities, accounts, permissions, and lifecycle processes across business systems, with an understanding of identity providers, MFA, SSO, SCIM, and centralised access management.

SaaS & business systems administration: Experience managing and optimising SaaS platforms, including user access, configuration, integrations, and documentation, with an interest in reducing complexity and unmanaged technology sprawl.

Security-aligned IT operations: Familiarity with security controls relevant to IT operations — device compliance, endpoint protection, identity governance, data protection, and application visibility — without needing to be a security specialist.

Systems integration & process improvement: Experience reviewing workflows, identifying inefficiencies, and delivering practical improvements that connect systems, reduce manual effort, and make operations more scalable.

Documentation & technical communication: Able to produce clear documentation, procedures, and user guidance, adapting communication style for technical and non-technical audiences alike.

Security & compliance awareness: Familiarity with security frameworks and how organisations implement security controls, with comfort working in environments where IT supports security, auditability, and customer trust.

Qualifications & certifications: Relevant IT qualifications or equivalent experience are valued. IMPORTANT NOTES: Your primary residence is considered your official duty station. TRAVEL STATEMENT: You may be required to travel to a disaster site during increased disaster activity for extended periods with little or no advanced notice.

This means that employees are in a pay and duty status only when activated to respond to workload needs, especially in response to heightened disaster activity. * Wir sind ein familiengeführtes, engagiertes Unternehmen mit einer nachhaltigen Vision.
* Wir fördern lebenslanges Lernen mit vielseitigen Schulungs- und Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten, internem Wissenstransfer und E-Learning.

## Mission ##
Le Technicien IT Support & Logistique est responsable de la préparation, de l'installation, du déplacement et de la maintenance du matériel informatique de l'entreprise. Il assure le support logistique lié aux postes de travail et participe aux projets de déménagement, d'aménagement et de renouvellement des équipements afin de garantir un environnement de travail fonctionnel pour les collaborateurs.
## Responsabilités principales ##
* Préparer, configurer et installer les postes de travail (PC, écrans, stations d'accueil, périphériques).
* Installer, remplacer et mettre à niveau les écrans et autres équipements informatiques.
* Désinstaller et réinstaller les équipements lors des changements de postes ou de réorganisations.
* Participer aux déménagements de bureaux et aux projets d'aménagement des espaces de travail.
* Déplacer le matériel informatique entre les différents sites ou services.
* Assurer le câblage de base des postes de travail (alimentation, réseau, périphériques).
* Effectuer les inventaires et maintenir à jour le stock de matériel informatique.
* Préparer le matériel pour les nouveaux collaborateurs et récupérer les équipements lors des départs.
* Diagnostiquer les problèmes matériels simples et remplacer les équipements défectueux.
* Coordonner la collecte, le recyclage et la mise au rebut du matériel informatique selon les procédures en vigueur.
* Veiller à la bonne organisation des zones de stockage du matériel IT.
* Collaborer avec l'équipe informatique pour les déploiements de masse et les projets d'infrastructure.
* Documenter les interventions et mettre à jour les outils de suivi.
## Compétences requises ##
* Bonne connaissance du matériel informatique (PC, écrans, imprimantes, stations d'accueil, accessoires).
* Connaissances de base en environnement Windows et Microsoft 365.
* Capacité à installer et connecter des équipements réseau et périphériques.
* Sens de l'organisation et rigueur dans la gestion du matériel.
* Bonne condition physique permettant la manipulation et le transport d'équipements.
* Esprit d'équipe et sens du service.
* Autonomie, flexibilité et capacité à gérer plusieurs interventions simultanément.
## Profil recherché ##
* Formation en informatique, support technique ou expérience équivalente.
* Une première expérience en support informatique de proximité ou en logistique IT est un atout.
* Permis de conduire (selon les besoins de l'entreprise).
* Maîtrise du français ; l'anglais technique constitue un avantage.
## Qualités personnelles ##
* Sens du service client.
* Organisation et méthode.
* Réactivité.
* Polyvalence.
* Esprit pratique et capacité à résoudre les problèmes.
* Bonne communication avec les utilisateurs et les équipes internes.
